card: Tracks in-flight manual P2P connection attempts in CConnman to prevent duplicate connections to the same target. Concurrent manual connection attempts—such as `-connect` and `-addnode` specifying the same destination during startup—race past existing duplicate checks because those checks only inspect peers already added to `m_nodes`. Target addresses and hostnames are now reserved during `OpenNetworkConnection()` so concurrent attempts are rejected while a dial is pending. This addresses long-standing issue #5299 with a new functional test reproducing the race condition.
changed_since_previous: Dropped changes to `ThreadOpenAddedConnections()`, leaving the addnode scheduler untouched. Connection reservation is now scoped strictly inside `OpenNetworkConnection()` via an RAII guard.
evidence: Addresses issue #5299 ('Initial connection management'), which reported duplicate manual connections during initial node startup.

PR description: '-connect and -addnode can attempt the same manual connection concurrently during startup. The existing duplicate checks cannot see a peer until it has been added to m_nodes, so both attempts can pass and open connections.'
Adds a functional test in `test/functional/p2p_duplicate_manual_connections.py` verifying that holding a connection attempt during a proxy handshake blocks duplicate connection attempts.
problem: Concurrent manual connection attempts to the same target—such as overlapping `-connect` and `-addnode` parameters during startup or concurrent `addnode onetry` calls—can race past duplicate checks. Because existing checks only inspect peers already published to `m_nodes`, multiple connections to the same remote peer can be established before either completes its handshake.

risk.why: Flaws in the destination reservation tracking could fail to release keys or mismatch addresses, blocking valid manual connections and reconnections.

summary: Tracks in-flight manual P2P connection attempts in `CConnman` using a set of pending destination keys to prevent duplicate connections. When `OpenNetworkConnection()` initiates a manual connection, it registers the target in `m_manual_connection_in_progress` and clears it upon exit using an RAII guard. Secondary attempts to the same numeric address or hostname string while an attempt is already dialing are rejected.
